rubric_definition: After you make the edit that one reviewer is asking for, does the other reviewer's comment still stand? If it is discharged too, the two findings are one defect; if it survives, they are different defects that share a location. If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.

panel.summary: note-sync now opens a Yorkie `doc.update` on EVERY docChanged ViewUpdate, including read-only mounts reacting to remote changes
panel.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts:61 wraps the whole loop in `this.store.batch(() => {...})`, and `YorkieNoteStore.batch()` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:76) unconditionally calls `this.doc.update(...)` before any transaction filtering. Previously, a read-only mount could never reach `doc.update` from this plugin: `editText` was only called for non-remote user-event transactions, which a non-editable view cannot produce. The out-of-diff consumer is packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:91, whose comment records the invariant that read-only share viewers must not issue writes ('a read-only share viewer has no write permission — the auth webhook would reject the update'). Now every peer edit or snapshot arriving at a read-only viewer opens a local (empty) update. Mitigating: `setLocalSelection` (remote-selection.ts:115) already calls doc.update on read-only mounts for presence, and the task note claims an empty update pushes nothing — hence low confidence. Fix belongs in YorkieNoteStore.batch (skip doc.update when nothing will be written) or in note-sync (only open a batch when at least one local transaction survives the filter).
